questions.q: Which field do most orgs group by to build a commit / best case / pipeline view of the quarter?
options: Forecast Category
Lead Source
Record Type
Created Date
questions.explain: Forecast Category is normally set from the Stage and is the natural grouping for a forecast ladder report.

questions.q: Why can't a standard Opportunity report simply divide open pipeline by quota to show coverage?
options: Reports cannot use division at all
Quota is not a field on the Opportunity, so the target has to come from a custom field or a dashboard gauge goal
Coverage is only defined for closed opportunities
Pipeline amounts are hidden from reports
questions.explain: Quota lives with the forecasting feature. Analysts usually store a target on a custom field or set it as a gauge goal on the dashboard.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the Forecasts page versus a forecast report?
options: They are identical and interchangeable
Reports roll up the hierarchy and support manager adjustments; the Forecasts page is for slicing
The Forecasts page suits the weekly roll-up and adjustments; reports suit slicing by other fields
The Forecasts page replaces the need for any opportunity reports
questions.explain: The Forecasts page is built for the hierarchy roll-up and adjustments. Reports let you slice by product, source, owner and more.

questions.q: Why is forecast accuracy harder to measure natively than the forecast itself?
options: Accuracy needs the number as it stood at the start of the period, and reports show current data unless history is captured
Closed Won opportunities are removed from reports
Accuracy can only be measured by an administrator in Setup
Forecast Category cannot be reported on
questions.explain: You must capture the earlier commit number (via historical trending where available, a snapshot, or a custom record) to compare it with actual results.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, $3.0M of open pipeline against $1.0M still needed gives what coverage?
questions.explain: Coverage is open pipeline divided by the remaining target: 3.0 / 1.0 = 3.0x. (Example numbers only.)
